p.src: As our story goes, it was nearly the end of the fourth watch before Lin Daiyu gradually fell asleep. We shall leave her there for now. Let us now turn to Xifeng. When Lady Xing sent for her, she had no idea what the matter was, so she hurriedly changed her clothes and ornaments and came over by carriage. Lady Xing dismissed everyone from the room and said quietly to Xifeng, “I did not call you here about anything else. The master has entrusted me with a difficult matter, and as I cannot decide what to do, I wanted to consult you first. The master has taken a fancy to the old lady’s maid Yuanyang and wants her in his chamber, so he has told me to ask the old lady for her. I suppose there is nothing unusual in that, but I am afraid the old lady will refuse. Can you think of a way?” On hearing this, Xifeng hastily replied, “If you ask me, you had better not court such a rebuff. The old lady can scarcely eat without Yuanyang. How could she possibly bear to give her up? Besides, whenever the subject comes up in ordinary conversation, the old lady often says that the master is getting on in years and ought not to keep taking one young concubine after another into his rooms and needlessly ruin their lives. Instead of taking care of his health or attending properly to his official duties, he spends every day drinking with his concubines. Do you imagine she is pleased with the master when she says such things? At a time when you cannot keep out of trouble fast enough, you would instead be poking a straw straight into a tiger’s nostril! Please do not be angry, madam, but I would not dare undertake it. It plainly cannot succeed and will only bring humiliation upon us. The master is advanced in years now, and when he acts improperly, you ought to advise him against it. He is no longer young enough for such conduct to pass without consequence. With all his brothers, nephews, sons, and grandsons around him, how can he face anyone if he still makes such a commotion?” Lady Xing gave a cold laugh. “Plenty of men in great families have three wives and four concubines. Why should ours alone be forbidden? Even if I advised him, he would not necessarily listen. Even though she is the old lady’s favorite maid, her eldest son is a grey-bearded man and an official besides. If he asks to take the girl as a chamber companion, she can hardly refuse him outright. I called you here merely to discuss it, yet you have already delivered a whole sermon on what is wrong with it. Who ever said that you were to ask for her? Naturally, I shall speak to her myself. You accuse me of failing to advise him, but you do not know his temper: before I could persuade him, he would first become angry with me.”

p.src: Xifeng knew that Lady Xing was foolish and obstinate by nature. Her first concern was to secure her position by yielding to Jia She in everything, and her second was to gratify herself by grasping after money and possessions; every affair in the household, great or small, was governed by Jia She. Whenever money passed through her hands, she was extraordinarily stingy, claiming that Jia She was so extravagant that “I must economize wherever I can to make up for it.” She trusted neither children nor servants and would listen to no one. Hearing Lady Xing speak in this fashion now, Xifeng realized that her perversity had once more asserted itself and that advice was useless. She therefore hastened to smile ingratiatingly and say, “What you say is perfectly right, madam. How old am I, after all, and what do I know of what matters and what does not? When it comes to parents, let alone a mere maid, even the greatest living treasure should be given to the master rather than to anyone else. How could one ever believe things said in private? I truly am a fool. When Second Master Lian does something wrong, the master and you may hate him so bitterly that you wish he could be dragged in and beaten to death on the spot; yet once you see him, the matter is dropped, and you still reward him with things you both treasure. Naturally, the old lady feels the same way toward the master. In my opinion, since the old lady is in good spirits today, today is the very day to ask her. I shall go ahead and amuse the old lady until she laughs. When you arrive, I shall make some excuse to slip away and take everyone else in the room with me, so that you can speak to her privately. If she grants the request, so much the better; if she refuses, no harm will be done, and no one else will know.” Lady Xing was pleased again by these words and told her, “My idea is not to ask the old lady first. If the old lady says no, the whole matter will be finished. I intend first to speak quietly to Yuanyang herself. Though she will be shy, if I explain everything carefully, she will naturally say nothing, and the matter will be settled. Then I shall speak to the old lady. Even if she objects, she cannot keep the girl against her will. As the saying goes, ‘Those determined to leave cannot be detained.’ The matter will naturally be settled.” Xifeng laughed. “You are indeed the clever one, madam. That plan is absolutely certain to succeed. Whether it is Yuanyang or anyone else, who would not wish to attach herself to someone powerful, rise in the world, and make something of herself? Would she refuse the chance to become half a mistress and prefer to remain a maid, only to be married off to some young servant in the end?” Lady Xing laughed. “Precisely so. Not only Yuanyang—even among the senior maids who hold responsible posts, which of them would not wish for such a thing? Go ahead of me, and do not breathe a word of this. I shall come over after supper.”

p.src: Xifeng thought to herself, “Yuanyang has always been a difficult creature. Despite what we have said, there is no assurance that she will agree. If I go first and madam comes later, nothing need be said if Yuanyang consents; but if she refuses, madam is so suspicious that she may think I leaked the secret and induced the girl to put on airs. Then, seeing that events have borne out my warning, madam will turn shame and vexation into anger and vent it upon me. That would be most unpleasant. It would be better for us to go together. Whether Yuanyang agrees or refuses, no suspicion can then fall upon me.” Having reached this conclusion, she smiled and said, “Just before I came, my aunt sent over two cages of quail. I told the servants to fry them, intending to have them brought here in time for your supper. As I entered the main gate just now, I saw the lads carrying away your carriage. They said that a joint had opened and that they were taking it to be repaired. Why do we not both take my carriage and go over now?” Lady Xing agreed and ordered her attendants to help her change her clothes. Xifeng busied herself attending to her for a while, after which the two women came over together in the carriage. Xifeng then said, “If I accompany you to the old lady’s quarters and she asks what I went to your place for, it will be awkward to answer. It would be better for you to go ahead while I change my clothes and follow later.”

p.src: Lady Xing saw the sense in this and went herself to Grandmother Jia's quarters. After chatting with her for a while, she came out on the pretext of going to Lady Wang's rooms, slipped out through the back gate, and passed by Yuanyang's bedroom. She found Yuanyang sitting there doing needlework. At the sight of Lady Xing, Yuanyang hurriedly rose. “What are you working on?” Lady Xing asked with a smile. “Let me see. Your embroidery is getting better and better.” As she spoke, she took the needlework from Yuanyang's hands, examined it, and praised it extravagantly. Then she put it down and looked Yuanyang over from head to toe. She was wearing a half-new silk jacket of pale lotus-root pink, a dark-blue satin vest with piping, and a light-green skirt. She had a slender waist and narrow shoulders, an oval face, glossy black hair, a high nose, and a faint sprinkling of freckles on both cheeks. Embarrassed by such close scrutiny, Yuanyang began to wonder what it meant and asked with a smile, “Madam, what brings you here at this odd hour?” Lady Xing gave a meaningful glance, and her attendants withdrew. Lady Xing sat down, took Yuanyang by the hand, and said smilingly, “I have come especially to congratulate you.” At these words, Yuanyang guessed something of her purpose. Her face reddened, and she lowered her head without saying a word. Lady Xing continued, “You know that your master has no truly dependable woman at his side. He has thought of buying another, but girls supplied by brokers may come from dubious backgrounds, and no one knows what faults they have. Once brought into the household, within a few days they may start playing all manner of outrageous tricks. “So he wanted to choose one of the household-born maids and take her into his rooms, but there was not a suitable one among them: one lacked looks, another had a bad disposition; each had one merit but lacked another. “He has therefore been quietly observing you all for half a year, and of all the girls, you alone stand out. In looks, conduct, character, gentleness, and trustworthiness, you have everything. “He means to ask the Old Lady for you and take you into his rooms. “You are not like some newly purchased girl from outside. As soon as you enter his household, your face will be threaded and you will be formally made a concubine—a position both respectable and distinguished. “You are ambitious too. As the saying goes, ‘Only gold is worthy in exchange for gold.’ Who would have thought the master would take such a fancy to you? “Now your long-standing hopes of rising in the world can be fulfilled, and you can silence those who have looked down on you. “Come with me to see the Old Lady!” With that, she took Yuanyang's hand and tried to lead her away. Yuanyang blushed and tried unsuccessfully to pull her hand free. Lady Xing, supposing that she was merely shy, said, “What is there to be embarrassed about? “You need not say anything; you have only to come with me.” Yuanyang merely lowered her head and would not move.

p.src: Seeing her like this, Lady Xing said again, “Surely you do not mean that you are unwilling? “If you truly are unwilling, then you really are a foolish girl. “You could become a mistress, yet you would rather remain a maid! “In another two or three years, at most they will marry you to some servant lad, and you will still be a slave. “If you come with us, you know I am good-natured and not the sort of woman who cannot tolerate another. “And the master treats the women in his rooms well. “Within a year or so, if you bear him a son or daughter, you will stand shoulder to shoulder with me. “Then, whoever in the household you choose to command, who would dare disobey? “Why turn your back on the chance to become a mistress? If you let this opportunity pass, it will be too late for regrets.” Yuanyang kept her head bowed and still said nothing. Lady Xing continued, “You are usually so frank and forthright. Why have you suddenly become so hesitant and tongue-tied? “If there is anything that does not please you, just tell me. I promise to see that everything is arranged to your satisfaction.” Yuanyang remained silent. Lady Xing smiled again. “No doubt you have parents, and you are too shy to speak for yourself. “You want to wait until they ask you. That is only proper. “Let me go and speak to them. I shall have them come and ask you, and then you may tell them whatever you wish.” Having said this, she went to Xifeng's rooms.

p.src: After Lady Xing had gone, Yuanyang was certain she had gone to discuss the matter in Xifeng’s rooms and that someone would surely come to question her. Thinking it best to hide, she found Hupo and said, “If the Old Lady asks for me, just say I felt ill, ate no breakfast, and went for a stroll in the garden, but will soon be back.” Hupo agreed. Yuanyang then went into the garden and wandered about until, quite unexpectedly, she ran into Pinger. Seeing that no one else was there, Pinger laughed and said, “Here comes the new concubine!” Yuanyang blushed when she heard this and said, “So that is why you all conspired together to scheme against me! Just wait—I shall go and have it out with your mistress.” Pinger regretted her careless words as soon as she heard this. Taking Yuanyang beneath a maple tree, she sat with her on a rock and told her the entire story—everything Xifeng had said and done before and after her visit, and how the affair had arisen. Her face flushed, Yuanyang gave Pinger a cold smile. “We have always been close—Xiren, Hupo, Suyun, Zijuan, Caixia, Yuchuan, Sheyue, Cuimo, Cuilü who went with Miss Shi, Keren and Jinchuan who are dead, Qianxue who left, and you and I besides. There are more than a dozen of us. Ever since childhood, what have we not talked about? What have we not done together? Now that we have all grown up, each has gone her own way, yet my feelings remain unchanged, and I still conceal none of my affairs or thoughts from any of you. For now, keep this to yourself and do not tell Mistress Lian: even if the Master did not merely want me as his concubine—even if his wife died this very moment and he sought to marry me as his lawful wife with all the proper matchmakers and betrothal gifts—I still would not go to him.”

p.src: Pinger was just about to answer with a laugh when a peal of laughter came from behind the rockery. “What a shameless girl! How can you say such things without setting your own teeth on edge?” The two girls started in alarm, hurriedly rose, and searched behind the rocks. It was none other than Xiren, who emerged laughing and asked, “What is this about? Tell me.” As she spoke, the three of them sat down on the rock. Pinger repeated the conversation to Xiren and said, “Strictly speaking, we ought not to say this, but the Master is truly far too lecherous. If a woman has even passably regular features, he will not leave her alone.” Pinger continued, “Since you do not wish it, I will teach you a way to settle the matter without any trouble.” “What way?” asked Yuanyang. “Tell me, and let me hear it.” Pinger laughed. “Just tell the Old Lady that you have already been given to Second Master Lian. Then the Master will be in no position to demand you.” Yuanyang spat contemptuously. “What nonsense! How can you still say such a thing? Did your mistress not babble the same nonsense the other day? Who would have thought it would come true today!” Xiren laughed. “Since neither of them wants you, I shall speak to the Old Lady and ask her to say that you have already been promised to Baoyu. Then the Master will give up all hope.” Angry, embarrassed, and exasperated all at once, Yuanyang cursed them. “You two wretched little hussies! May you come to no good end! When a person is in trouble and trusts you as sensible women, hoping you will help her find a way out, you take turns making fun of her instead. You imagine that your own futures are settled and that you will both become concubines one day. But as I see it, things in this world do not always turn out as one wishes. You had better restrain yourselves and not rejoice too soon!” Seeing that she was truly upset, the two hastened to placate her with apologetic smiles. “Dear sister, do not take it to heart. We have been as close as real sisters since childhood; we merely made a little joke because no one else was here. Tell us what you intend to do, so that we may set our minds at ease.” “What do I intend?” said Yuanyang. “I simply will not go, and that is the end of it.” Pinger shook her head. “Your refusal may not be enough to put an end to it. You know the Master’s temper. Though you belong to the Old Lady’s household and he dares not do anything to you now, surely you cannot stay with her forever? One day you will have to leave. If you fall into his hands then, matters will be worse.” Yuanyang smiled coldly. “As long as the Old Lady lives, I shall never leave this place. If she passes away, he will still have three years of mourning to observe. Surely he cannot take a concubine before his own mother is scarcely dead! After three years, who knows how circumstances may have changed? We can speak of it again then.

Angry, embarrassed, and exasperated all at once, Yuanyang cursed them. “You two wretched little hussies! May you come to no good end!
When a person is in trouble and trusts you as sensible women, hoping you will help her find a way out, you take turns making fun of her instead.
You imagine that your own futures are settled and that you will both become concubines one day.
But as I see it, things in this world do not always turn out as one wishes.
You had better restrain yourselves and not rejoice too soon!”

Seeing that she was truly upset, the two hastened to placate her with apologetic smiles. “Dear sister, do not take it to heart. We have been as close as real sisters since childhood; we merely made a little joke because no one else was here.
Tell us what you intend to do, so that we may set our minds at ease.”
“What do I intend?” said Yuanyang.
“I simply will not go, and that is the end of it.”
Pinger shook her head. “Your refusal may not be enough to put an end to it.
You know the Master’s temper.
Though you belong to the Old Lady’s household and he dares not do anything to you now, surely you cannot stay with her forever?
One day you will have to leave.
If you fall into his hands then, matters will be worse.”

Yuanyang smiled coldly. “As long as the Old Lady lives, I shall never leave this place. If she passes away, he will still have three years of mourning to observe. Surely he cannot take a concubine before his own mother is scarcely dead!
After three years, who knows how circumstances may have changed? We can speak of it again then.

p.src: Even if I am driven to the utmost extremity, I can cut off my hair and become a nun—or, failing that, I can still die. What would be so terrible about never marrying a man in my whole life? I should be glad to remain unencumbered!” Pinger and Xiren laughed. “This shameless hussy truly has no sense of modesty left—now she is blurting out absolutely anything!” Yuanyang replied, “With matters come to this, what does a moment’s embarrassment matter? If you do not believe me, just wait and see. Her Ladyship has just said that she will seek out my parents. Let us see her go all the way to Nanjing to find them!” Pinger said, “Your parents are both in Nanjing looking after the family property and have not come north, but sooner or later she will find them. Besides, your elder brother and sister-in-law are here now. Unfortunately, you were born a bondservant of this household; you are not like the two of us, who entered its service on our own.” “What if I was born a bondservant?” said Yuanyang. “Can they force an ox’s head down when it will not drink? If I refuse, can they possibly kill my parents?”

p.src: As they were speaking, they saw her sister-in-law coming toward them from across the way. Xiren said, “When they could not find your parents, they must have spoken to your sister-in-law.” Yuanyang said, “That whore is a born busybody—a veritable ‘camel peddler among nine kingdoms.’ Once she heard of this, do you suppose she would fail to curry favor with them?” While they were still speaking, she had already reached them. Her sister-in-law said with a smile, “I searched everywhere for you, and here you are, miss!” Come with me; I have something to tell you.” Ping’er and Xiren both hastened to offer her a seat. Her sister-in-law said, “You young ladies please remain seated. I only came to say a word to our girl.” Xiren and Ping’er pretended not to understand and said with smiles, “What could be so urgent? We are guessing riddles here, with slaps on the hand as the stakes. Let her finish this one before she goes.” Yuanyang asked, “What is it? Tell me here.” Her sister-in-law replied with a smile, “Come with me and I will tell you when we get there. In any case, it is good news.” Yuanyang asked, “Is it what the First Lady spoke to you about?” Her sister-in-law laughed. “Since you already know, why make things difficult for me? Come quickly and let me explain it all to you. It is an enormous piece of good fortune.” At this, Yuanyang sprang to her feet, spat with all her might straight into her sister-in-law’s face, pointed at her, and cursed, “Clamp that filthy cunt of a mouth shut and get out of here while you still can! What ‘good words’! Emperor Huizong’s hawks and Zhao Mengfu’s horses—those are good paintings! What ‘happy event’! When the top scholar’s smallpox pustules fill with matter, that too is nothing but a ‘happy event’! No wonder you are always envying families whose daughters become concubines, so that the whole household can rely on them to swagger and bully others—as if every last one of them had become a concubine! Your eyes grew hot with envy, so now you mean to send me into the fire pit as well. If I won favor, you would swagger about outside, bullying everyone, and appoint yourselves the master’s honored in-laws. But if I lost favor and came to ruin, you turtles would pull in your necks and leave me to live or die as fate decreed.” She wept as she spoke, while Ping’er and Xiren restrained and consoled her. Her sister-in-law, unable to save face, said, “Whether you want it or not, you could say so civilly. There is no call to drag other people into it. As the saying goes, ‘Do not speak of shortness in front of a dwarf.’ If my fine young lady curses me, I dare not answer back; but these two young ladies have done nothing to offend you. How can they hold up their heads when you keep talking of concubines this and concubines that?” Xiren and Ping’er hastily said, “Do not speak like that. She was not referring to us, so do not drag other people into it yourself. Have you ever heard any lady or master appoint us as concubines? Besides, neither of us has parents or brothers serving in this household who could rely on us to swagger and bully others.

p.src: Yuanyang was still so angry that she continued cursing, and only stopped after Ping’er and Xiren had soothed her for some time. Ping’er then asked Xiren, “What were you doing hiding over there? We never saw you at all.” Xiren replied, “I had gone to Fourth Miss’s rooms to look for our Master Bao, but I arrived a step too late and was told that he had come home. I wondered how I could have missed him and thought of looking for him at Miss Lin’s, but then I met one of her people, who said he had not gone there either. I was standing here wondering whether he had left the garden when, as chance would have it, you came from over there. I slipped aside, and you did not see me. Then she came along as well. I moved from behind this tree to the rocks behind the artificial hill, and then I saw you two talking. Who would have thought that your four eyes would fail to see me?”

p.src: Before she had finished, they heard someone behind them laugh and say, “Their four eyes did not see you? Why, all six of your eyes failed to see me!” The three of them jumped in alarm. They turned and saw none other than Baoyu approaching. Xiren was the first to laugh. “You have made me search everywhere! Where have you been?” Baoyu replied with a smile, “When I came out of Fourth Sister’s place, I saw you approaching. I knew at once that you were coming to look for me, so I hid to play a trick on you. I watched you go past with your head lowered, enter the courtyard, come straight out again, and question everyone you met. I found it very amusing and meant to wait until you came near, then give you a fright. But afterward, when I saw you creeping about and hiding too, I knew that you also meant to play a trick on someone. I poked my head out and looked ahead, and saw that it was those two, so I circled around behind you. When you came out, I hid in the very place where you had been hiding.” Ping’er laughed. “Let us search farther back. Who knows? We may yet find another two people.” Baoyu laughed. “No, there really is no one else.” Yuanyang knew that Baoyu had overheard everything they had said, so she merely lay face down on the rock and pretended to sleep. Baoyu nudged her and said with a smile, “This rock is cold. Would it not be better for us to go back inside and sleep?” As he spoke, he pulled Yuanyang to her feet, then promptly invited Ping’er to come to his rooms for tea. Ping’er and Xiren both urged Yuanyang to come along. Only then did she rise, and all four proceeded to Happy Red Court. Baoyu had heard every word of the preceding conversation and was naturally distressed. He lay silently on the bed while the three young women talked and laughed in the outer room.

p.src: Meanwhile, Lady Xing asked Xifeng about Yuanyang's parents, and Xifeng replied, “Her father's name is Jin Cai. He and his wife look after the houses in Nanjing and seldom come to the capital. Her elder brother, Jin Wenxiang, is now the Lady Dowager's purchasing agent. Her sister-in-law is also the head laundress in the Lady Dowager's household.” Lady Xing therefore sent for Yuanyang's sister-in-law, Jin Wenxiang's wife, and explained the matter to her in detail. Jin Wenxiang's wife was naturally delighted. She hurried eagerly to find Yuanyang, certain that one word from her would settle everything. Instead, Yuanyang sharply rebuked her, and Xiren and Ping'er added a few remarks of their own. Humiliated and angry, she returned and told Lady Xing, “It's no use. She gave me a fine scolding instead.” Since Xifeng was present, she dared not mention Ping'er and said only, “Xiren joined her in rebuking me and said many impertinent things that ought never to be repeated to a mistress. Madam had better discuss with Master the purchase of another girl. I suppose that little wretch was never blessed with such good fortune, nor were we fortunate enough to bring this about.” Hearing this, Lady Xing said, “What has any of this to do with Xiren? How did they come to know about it?” Then she asked, “Who else was there?” Jin Wenxiang's wife replied, “Miss Ping'er was there too.” Xifeng hastily cried, “Why didn't you slap her face and drag her back here? The moment I step out, she goes roaming about, and when I come home I cannot find so much as her shadow! She must have joined in and said something too!” Jin Wenxiang's wife said, “Miss Ping'er was not actually nearby. From a distance the figure looked like her, but I could not see clearly. It was only my own guess.” Xifeng ordered a servant, “Go and fetch her at once. Tell her I am home and Madam is here too, and ask her to come and lend a hand.” Feng'er hurried forward and reported, “Miss Lin sent someone with a formal invitation three or four times before she finally went. I sent for her as soon as you came through the door, Madam. Miss Lin said, ‘Tell your mistress that I need her for something.’” Only then did Xifeng let the matter drop, though she deliberately added, “She is forever sending for her. What can she possibly need her for?”

p.src: Lady Xing could think of no other plan. After dinner she returned home and told Jia She about it that evening. After thinking for a moment, Jia She immediately summoned Jia Lian and said, “There are others looking after our properties in Nanjing, and more than one household at that. Send for Jin Cai at once.” Jia Lian replied, “The last letter from Nanjing said that Jin Cai had already become delirious from phlegm clouding his mind. Money for his coffin has even been granted there. No one knows whether he is alive or dead now, and even if he is alive, he is insensible, so summoning him would be useless. Besides, his old wife is deaf.” At this Jia She gave an angry shout and cursed, “You lowborn bastard! Trust you to know all about it! Get out of my sight!” Jia Lian withdrew in terror. Before long, Jia She ordered Jin Wenxiang to be summoned. Jia Lian remained in attendance in the outer study. He dared neither go home nor face his father, and could only listen from there. Presently Jin Wenxiang arrived. The young pages led him straight through the second gate, and only after the time it would take to eat five or six meals did he come out and leave. Jia Lian did not dare make inquiries just then. After a while he learned that Jia She had gone to sleep, and only then did he come back inside. It was not until Xifeng told him that evening that he finally understood what had happened.

p.src: Yuanyang did not sleep all night. The next day, her brother reported to the Lady Dowager that he wished to take her home for a visit. The Lady Dowager consented and told Yuanyang to go out. Yuanyang did not want to go, but feared that the Lady Dowager might become suspicious, so she had no choice but to come out reluctantly. Her brother then had no choice but to relay Jia She's words to her, promising how honorably she would be treated and how, as a concubine, she would manage the household. Yuanyang clenched her teeth and steadfastly refused. Her brother could do nothing more and had to report back to Jia She. Jia She flew into a rage and said, “Mark what I tell you. Have your wife speak to her and repeat my very words: ‘Since ancient times, Chang'e has loved the young.’ She must think me too old and is probably enamored of the young masters. Most likely she has set her heart on Baoyu, though Jia Lian may be another possibility. If she does harbor such thoughts, tell her to abandon them at once. If I want her and she refuses to come to me, who would dare take her afterward? That is the first point. Second, she may be counting on the Lady Dowager's fondness for her, thinking that in time the old lady will naturally marry her outside the household as a man's lawful wife. Tell her to think carefully: no matter whom she marries, she will find it hard to escape the palm of my hand. Unless she dies or never marries a man for the rest of her life, I shall never concede defeat to her! Otherwise, tell her to change her mind while there is still time, for she stands to gain many advantages.” At every sentence Jia She spoke, Jin Wenxiang answered, “Yes.” Jia She said, “Do not try to deceive me. Tomorrow I shall send your mistress over to question Yuanyang again. If you have spoken to her and she still refuses, the fault will not lie with either of you. But if, when she is asked, she then agrees, you had better watch your head!”

p.src: As it happened, Lady Wang, Aunt Xue, Li Wan, Xifeng, Baochai and the other young ladies, together with several respectable wives of the senior stewards from outside, were all amusing Grandmother Jia. Yuanyang was overjoyed. Pulling her sister-in-law with her, she knelt before Grandmother Jia and, weeping as she spoke, related what Lady Xing had said to her, what her sister-in-law had said in the garden, and what her brother had told her that day. “Because I refused, the Master has now gone so far as to say that I am in love with Baoyu. Otherwise, he says, I must be hoping to marry outside. Even if I flew up to heaven, I could never escape his grasp in this lifetime, and sooner or later he would take revenge. I have made up my mind. Before everyone here I swear that in this lifetime, let alone a ‘Precious Jade,’ even if he were ‘Precious Gold,’ ‘Precious Silver,’ a ‘Precious Heavenly King,’ or a ‘Precious Emperor,’ I will never marry anyone at all! Even if Her Ladyship herself tried to force me, I would cut my throat rather than obey! If fortune favors me, I shall die before Her Ladyship. If not, and I am fated to become a beggar, then after serving Her Ladyship until she passes away, I still will not return to my parents and brother. I shall either kill myself or cut off my hair and become a nun! If I am not sincere, if I am only making excuses for now while secretly planning something else later, then let Heaven and Earth, ghosts and spirits, the sun and moon bear witness: may a boil grow in my throat, rot its way outward, and reduce me here to a pool of putrid flesh!” In fact, when she entered she had concealed a pair of scissors in her sleeve. Even as she spoke, she loosened her hair with her left hand and began cutting it with her right. The old women and maids rushed to restrain her, but half a lock had already been cut off. Fortunately, when they looked, they saw that her hair was so thick that the scissors had not cut all the way through, and they hurriedly dressed it again for her. When Grandmother Jia heard this, her whole body shook with rage, and she could only keep saying, “I have just this one dependable person left, and still they scheme to take her from me!” Seeing Lady Wang beside her, she turned to her and said, “So all of you have been deceiving me! You show me respect to my face while plotting against me in secret. Whenever I have something good, you want it; whenever I have a good servant, you want her too. Now only this little slip of a girl remains, and because you see that I treat her well, naturally you cannot bear it. You mean to get rid of her so that you can manipulate me as you please!” Lady Wang hastily rose and dared not answer a word. Aunt Xue saw that even Lady Wang had been blamed and found it all the harder to intervene. As soon as Li Wan heard what Yuanyang was saying, she had already led the young ladies outside.

u.src: As it happened, Lady Wang, Aunt Xue, Li Wan, Xifeng, Baochai and the other young ladies, together with several respectable wives of the senior stewards from outside, were all amusing Grandmother Jia.

Yuanyang was overjoyed. Pulling her sister-in-law with her, she knelt before Grandmother Jia and, weeping as she spoke, related what Lady Xing had said to her, what her sister-in-law had said in the garden, and what her brother had told her that day. “Because I refused, the Master has now gone so far as to say that I am in love with Baoyu. Otherwise, he says, I must be hoping to marry outside. Even if I flew up to heaven, I could never escape his grasp in this lifetime, and sooner or later he would take revenge.

I have made up my mind. Before everyone here I swear that in this lifetime, let alone a ‘Precious Jade,’ even if he were ‘Precious Gold,’ ‘Precious Silver,’ a ‘Precious Heavenly King,’ or a ‘Precious Emperor,’ I will never marry anyone at all!
Even if Her Ladyship herself tried to force me, I would cut my throat rather than obey!

If fortune favors me, I shall die before Her Ladyship. If not, and I am fated to become a beggar, then after serving Her Ladyship until she passes away, I still will not return to my parents and brother. I shall either kill myself or cut off my hair and become a nun!

If I am not sincere, if I am only making excuses for now while secretly planning something else later, then let Heaven and Earth, ghosts and spirits, the sun and moon bear witness: may a boil grow in my throat, rot its way outward, and reduce me here to a pool of putrid flesh!”
In fact, when she entered she had concealed a pair of scissors in her sleeve. Even as she spoke, she loosened her hair with her left hand and began cutting it with her right.
The old women and maids rushed to restrain her, but half a lock had already been cut off.
Fortunately, when they looked, they saw that her hair was so thick that the scissors had not cut all the way through, and they hurriedly dressed it again for her.
When Grandmother Jia heard this, her whole body shook with rage, and she could only keep saying, “I have just this one dependable person left, and still they scheme to take her from me!”

You show me respect to my face while plotting against me in secret.

Whenever I have something good, you want it; whenever I have a good servant, you want her too. Now only this little slip of a girl remains, and because you see that I treat her well, naturally you cannot bear it. You mean to get rid of her so that you can manipulate me as you please!”
Lady Wang hastily rose and dared not answer a word.
Aunt Xue saw that even Lady Wang had been blamed and found it all the harder to intervene.
As soon as Li Wan heard what Yuanyang was saying, she had already led the young ladies outside.

p.src: Tanchun, who was quick-witted, reflected that although Lady Wang had been unjustly blamed, she could hardly defend herself; Aunt Xue was her own sister and naturally could not very well speak for her; Baochai could not properly defend her aunt; and Li Wan, Xifeng, and Baoyu all dared not say anything. This was precisely a moment when one of the girls was needed. Yingchun was too meek and Xichun too young, so after listening for a while outside the window, Tanchun entered and said to Grandmother Jia with a smile, “What has this affair to do with Mother? Think about it, Grandmother: if an elder brother-in-law wants to take someone into his chamber, how could his younger brother’s wife know about it? Even if she did know, she would have to pretend that she did not.” Before she had finished, Grandmother Jia laughed and said, “Indeed, I have grown muddle-headed with age! Do not laugh at me, Aunt Xue. This sister of yours is exceedingly filial to me, unlike my elder daughter-in-law, who thinks only of fearing her husband and merely goes through the motions before her mother-in-law. I have wronged her indeed.” Aunt Xue merely answered, “Yes,” and then added, “It is also quite natural for an old lady to be partial and love her younger son’s wife more.” “I am not partial!” said Grandmother Jia. Then she continued, “Baoyu, I unjustly blamed your mother. Why did you not remind me, instead of watching her suffer this wrong?” Baoyu smiled. “Could I take Mother’s side and accuse Uncle and Aunt? There was only one person here to take the blame. If my mother would not accept it, on whom else could it be laid? I would have claimed that I was at fault, but you would never have believed me.” Grandmother Jia laughed. “That makes sense too. Quickly kneel before your mother and say, ‘Please do not feel aggrieved, Mother. Grandmother is old, so forgive her for Baoyu’s sake.’” Hearing this, Baoyu hurried over and knelt down to speak, but Lady Wang quickly pulled him up with a smile, saying, “Get up, quickly! You absolutely must not do this. Surely you cannot apologize to me on Grandmother’s behalf?” At this, Baoyu hastily stood up. Grandmother Jia laughed again. “Xifeng did not remind me either.” Xifeng laughed. “I was not going to blame you, Grandmother, yet now you have found fault with me?” Hearing this, Grandmother Jia and all the others laughed. “Well, this is strange! Let us hear what I did wrong.” Xifeng replied, “Who told you to train your servants so well, Grandmother, making them as fresh and lovely as green spring onions? How can you blame anyone for wanting one? Fortunately, I am only a grandson’s wife. Had I been a grandson, I would have asked for her long ago instead of waiting until now.” Grandmother Jia laughed. “So it is my fault after all?” “Naturally it is your fault, Grandmother,” Xifeng replied with a laugh. Grandmother Jia laughed. “In that case, I do not want her either. You may take her away!” Xifeng said, “Let me cultivate enough merit in this life to be reborn as a man in the next; then I shall ask for her.”

p.src: Grandmother Jia laughed. “Take her away and put her in Lian’s chamber. Then we shall see whether that shameless father-in-law of yours still wants her!” Xifeng said, “Lian is not worthy of her. All he deserves is to muddle along with Ping’er and me, this pair of scorched rolls.” At this, everyone burst out laughing. A maid came to report, “The elder mistress has arrived.” Lady Wang hurried out to receive her. To learn what followed, read the next chapter.
